main-rh.title: Mathlib RH
main-rh.contract: Every nontrivial zeta zero distinct from the pole has real part one half.
main-rh.idea: The proof term supplied to Mathlib’s own proposition is rhOfAll.
main-rh.name: riemannHypothesis

main-zeta.title: Zeta in expanded form
main-zeta.contract: Every zero other than the negative even integers and the point one has real part one half.
main-zeta.idea: The second name uses the same proof term as riemannHypothesis.
main-zeta.name: riemannZeta_eq_zero_re

main-right.title: Nonvanishing right of one half
main-right.contract: For all positive moduli and all characters, L(s,χ) is nonzero for Re(s)>1/2, excluding the principal pole.
main-right.idea: The export gives allChi as the proof.
main-right.name: LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re

main-strip.title: Dirichlet GRH in the open strip
main-strip.contract: For every character of positive modulus, any zero with 0<Re(s)<1 satisfies Re(s)=1/2.
main-strip.idea: The second conjunct in claimAll supplies the critical-strip statement.
main-strip.name: LFunction_eq_zero_re

main-prim.title: Primitive critical-strip zeros
main-prim.contract: For every primitive character of positive modulus, all zeros in the open critical strip have real part one half.
main-prim.idea: The proof uses a dedicated primitive reflection argument.
main-prim.name: LFunction_eq_zero_re_of_isPrimitive

stmt-zeta.title: Zeta target type
stmt-zeta.contract: ∀ s∈ℂ, ζ(s)=0, s outside {−2(n+1)} for n∈ℕ and s≠1 imply Re(s)=1/2.
stmt-zeta.idea: Defines the expanded zeta proposition. The two zeta exports share its mathematical meaning.
stmt-zeta.name: RiemannZetaZerosOnLine

stmt-right.title: Half-plane target type
stmt-right.contract: ∀ N≠0, χ mod N, s∈ℂ, 1/2<Re(s) and (χ≠1 or s≠1) imply L(s,χ)≠0.
stmt-right.idea: The disjunction excludes only the principal-character pole at one.
stmt-right.name: DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf

stmt-strip.title: Dirichlet strip target type
stmt-strip.contract: ∀ N≠0, χ mod N, s∈ℂ, 0<Re(s)<1 and L(s,χ)=0 imply Re(s)=1/2.
stmt-strip.idea: All complex Dirichlet characters are quantified.
stmt-strip.name: DirichletLZerosOnLine

stmt-prim.title: Primitive strip target type
stmt-prim.contract: The preceding strip implication for each χ satisfying IsPrimitive.
stmt-prim.idea: The primitive hypothesis is a visible binder.
stmt-prim.name: PrimitiveDirichletLZerosOnLine

g-m.title: The weighted prime sum
g-m.contract: G_P(x)=Gζ(x) plus a finite weighted sum of real parts of twisted smoothed errors.
g-m.idea: The cyclic level gives every nontrivial primitive inducing character weight 1/(3o+1).
g-m.name: Formalism.HC.Level.Gm

window-def.title: Uniform families on power windows
window-def.contract: There exist eD,eL and ε₁>0 such that every 0<ε<ε₁ admits a tied family with whole windows of width λ.
window-def.idea: The loss exponents are uniform in epsilon. The family may vary with epsilon.
window-def.name: Formalism.HC.ChebyshevInequalityAtWindowScale

vv.title: Weighted lengths of local-global kernels
vv.contract: For all admissible local data, lengths are finite for 1≤e<t and every finite prime sum of log(ℓ) times the sum of these lengths is ≤B.
vv.idea: Finiteness precedes conversion of an extended natural length to an ordinary natural.
vv.name: UpperTheory.Top.VVle

vwin-def.title: The cohomological window
vwin-def.contract: For every ε∈(0,1/52) and admissible layer choice e(x), sufficiently large X and each prescribed pair q,d admit a window [Y,Y²] where VAt holds.
vwin-def.idea: The endpoint uses Ct=401. VAt bounds twists below floor(x^401) by sqrt(exp(x^ε)).
vwin-def.name: UpperTheory.Top.VWinAt

row-def.title: The local–global Galois row
row-def.contract: For a regular algebraic polarized cuspidal representation over a CM field and a prime ℓ, there exist a Galois representation, weight and Hodge–Tate multiset satisfying PropsB.
row-def.idea: The fields of PropsB specify continuity, semisimplicity, comparisons and weight relations.
row-def.name: UpperTheory.GalStar.Row0b

rh-all.title: The two zeta exports share a proof
rh-all.idea: Apply the zeta reducer to the closed Dirichlet half-plane theorem.
rh-all.name: rhOfAll

all-chi.title: All-character half-plane theorem
all-chi.idea: Re-export everyCharacter from the arithmetic development.
all-chi.name: allChi

crit-all.title: Primitive critical-line wrapper
crit-all.contract: For primitive χ, every open-strip zero has real part one half.
crit-all.idea: Apply the primitive reflection lemma using allChi.
crit-all.name: critAll

claim-all.title: Three endpoint propositions
claim-all.idea: Build the conjunction. Main projects its middle field. The other fields also appear in the term that constructs the bundle.
claim-all.name: claimAll

rh-every.title: Specialize at modulus one
rh-every.idea: At modulus one the Dirichlet L-function equals zeta. Supply its right-half-plane nonvanishing to rh_of_right.
rh-every.name: Formalism.VW.rh_of_every

rh-right.title: Reflect a zeta zero
rh-right.contract: Right-half-plane zeta nonvanishing away from one implies Mathlib RH.
rh-right.idea: The functional equation reflects a left-hand zero. Gamma and cosine factors are nonzero once zero and the negative even integers are excluded.
rh-right.name: Formalism.VW.rh_of_right

vw-crit.title: Reflect a primitive character
vw-crit.contract: EveryCharacter implies the primitive open-strip conclusion.
vw-crit.idea: The completed functional equation reflects the zero to the inverse character at 1−s.
vw-crit.name: Formalism.VW.critLine

gamma.title: Gamma factors in the strip
gamma.contract: For every character χ and Re(s)>0 its gamma factor at s is nonzero.
gamma.idea: Use the even and odd formulas and Gammaℝ nonvanishing in the positive half-plane.
gamma.name: Formalism.VW.gammaFactor_ne_zero

strip.title: Reflect an arbitrary character
strip.idea: Reduce a left-hand zero to its primitive inducing character, reflect it, then use h. A right-hand zero directly contradicts h.
strip.name: Claim.strip

prim-zero.title: Remove imprimitive Euler factors
prim-zero.contract: An imprimitive character zero in 0<Re(s)<1 gives a zero of its primitive inducing character.
prim-zero.idea: Change level. Every removed prime factor has the form 1−χ(p)p^(−s), with the second term of norm less than one.
prim-zero.name: Claim.prim_zero

factor.title: Nonzero removed Euler factor
factor.idea: Use the bound on the norm of a character and the strict decay of p^(−Re(s)).
factor.name: Claim.factor_ne_zero

prim-reflect.title: Transfer a primitive zero to 1−s
prim-reflect.contract: At an open-strip zero of a primitive ψ, its inverse has a zero at 1−s.
prim-reflect.idea: Use the completed functional equation and nonvanishing of gamma in the strip.
prim-reflect.name: Claim.prim_reflect

bundle-zeta.title: Zeta component of the conjunction
bundle-zeta.idea: Use strip at modulus one in the interior, established nonvanishing for Re(s)≥1, and completed zeta symmetry on the left.
bundle-zeta.name: Claim.zeta

every.title: Closed half-plane assembly
every.contract: EveryCharacter with no explicit arithmetic premise.
every.idea: The final line supplies a named producer for the local–global Galois row.
every.name: UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter

from-row.title: The half-plane theorem from one row
from-row.contract: Row0b with the specified local parameter convention implies EveryCharacter.
from-row.idea: The same h fills two fields in the literature-input record and produces the cohomological window.
from-row.name: UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter_of_row

row-prod.title: Producer of the Galois row
row-prod.contract: Row0b recT with no explicit global premise.
row-prod.idea: Feed the named theta-lift theorem to the conditional Galois construction.
row-prod.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.galoisLocalGlobalStrong_recParameter

row-geo.title: Galois representations from theta lifting
row-geo.idea: Apply the geometric realization theorem with the named weight-one source and the theta lift.
row-geo.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.galoisRepresentations_of_thetaLift

tlift.title: Theta-lift existence at high rank
tlift.contract: For the admissible CM data of TLiftK, for all sufficiently high dimensions and allowed weights a lift U′ exists.
tlift.idea: This named theorem supplies the high-dimensional lift required for Row0b.
tlift.name: UpperTheory.TP.K.tLiftK

geo-one.title: Weight-one geometric realization
geo-one.idea: Converts the stated weight-one realization into the geometric input to the row.
geo-one.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.geoOne_holds

rec.title: Existence of local Langlands parameters
rec.idea: Extend a parameter from the cuspidal representations and establish the local comparison fields.
rec.name: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.recTExists

lit.title: Assemble the automorphic inputs
lit.idea: Pass the eigenvalue and local-theta packages, local matching, covolumes, local Langlands and VWin to the seven-input implication.
lit.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.every_character_of_literature_of_vWin

open-record.title: Three fields in the literature input
open-record.contract: The record has fields Row, RecTExists and Row, in that order.
open-record.idea: The two row fields have the same Lean type. The closed caller inserts the same term in both places.
open-record.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.OpenLiteratureStatements

eigen-package.title: The unitary and eigenvalue package
eigen-package.idea: The record starts with cohomological, finite-field character, Hecke, Chebotarev, polarized Galois and base-change inputs. These are the P argument.
eigen-package.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published_results_eigen

theta-package.title: The local theta package
theta-package.idea: The record begins with Green series, Linnik, complex multiplication, mirabolic, branching and local representation inputs. These supply F.
theta-package.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published_results_first

hodge-package.title: The Hodge-bundle package
hodge-package.idea: The geometric record starts with toroidal compactification, volume, arithmetic intersection calculus and abelian de Rham data. It feeds the covolume producer.
hodge-package.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published_results_arithmetic

local-rec.title: The local parameter input at the call site
local-rec.contract: OpenLiteratureStatements imply RecTExists in the GL convention.
local-rec.idea: Apply the local correspondence comparison to the parameter field of O and the named local converse, depth-zero, reciprocity and multisegment ingredients.
local-rec.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.local_langlands_gl_recT_exists_of_literature

local-rec-proj.title: Read the parameter field
local-rec-proj.idea: Project the localLanglandsExists field of O.
local-rec-proj.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.local_langlands_recT_exists_of_literature

green.title: Regular characters yield the Green input
green.idea: Use Frobenius conjugacy of regular labels to associate finite general-linear-group characters to irreducible polynomial labels.
green.name: GlobalTheory.GreenBridge.green_of_regular

linked-two-three.title: Bind the estimates at 2 and 3
linked-two-three.contract: For local-global inputs, RecTExists and a compatible dependence parameter, the bounds at two and three hold on linked data.
linked-two-three.idea: Package the local bounds for every eligible family into a linked slot at this common parameter.
linked-two-three.name: UpperTheory.N.boundAtTwoThree_linked_of_recT

goal-shape.title: Apply the shape to the same chosen data
goal-shape.contract: For propositions V, NR, G and a class predicate N, take TopShapeAlt V NR N G, V, NR and HypsAlt N DefiniteSideCondition to G.
goal-shape.idea: For the primitive zero-free argument both auxiliary propositions are trivial. The concrete input is the chosen definite-side record.
goal-shape.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.forall_goal_of_shape_of_hyps

shape-fields.title: Supply the actual fields of the shape
shape-fields.contract: TopShapeAlt V NR N G with V, NR and HypsAlt N DefiniteSideCondition yields G.
shape-fields.idea: Extract the selection, base level, columns, rank and divisibility inputs, and pass the period, local and global fields to the shape.
shape-fields.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.goal_of_shape_of_hyps

tlift-def.title: Quantifiers of the theta lift
tlift-def.contract: For each admissible CM setup, n≥1 and X, there exists d₀; for each d≥d₀, permissible W, Hecke characters, weights and U, an IsLift witness U′ exists.
tlift-def.idea: The weight inequality is imposed after the choice of d. The lift has an explicit existential codomain.
tlift-def.name: UpperTheory.TP.TLiftK

theta-match.title: Match global integrals and local data
theta-match.idea: Theorem K combines Eisenstein-series and Siegel–Weil inputs to produce both comparison statements.
theta-match.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.theta_integrals_agree_and_local_matching_of_literature

covol.title: Produce the covolume bound
covol.contract: The named geometric, arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel and Hodge-bundle hypotheses imply CovolumeBoundOfX.
covol.idea: This supplies the covolume comparison used by the seven-input theorem. Its source signature lists the geometric and arithmetic hypotheses.
covol.name: SelfIntersectionVolumeEstimates.topCovolSlim2_use_alt_alt

seven.title: Seven inputs for every character
seven.contract: The seven groups of hypotheses imply EveryCharacter.
seven.idea: Construct the definite-side package, obtain a Green-character input, and invoke the primitive-to-all-character assembly.
seven.name: UpperTheory.Lit.every_character_of_theta_integrals_local_matching

definite.title: Build a nonempty definite-side package
definite.contract: Unitary, theta, matching, covolume, local-parameter and linked-bound data yield Nonempty (HypsAlt … DefiniteSideCondition).
definite.idea: Use test vectors, Fourier coefficient grids, linked bundles and a single choice of the maximum of two thresholds.
definite.name: UpperTheory.Lit.nonempty_hyps_definite_side_of_closed_bound

every-green.title: Pass from primitive to all characters
every-green.contract: Green ∧ VWin ∧ nonempty definite-side hypotheses imply EveryCharacter, written as three binders.
every-green.idea: Obtain primitive nonvanishing at cyclic levels and restore imprimitive factors.
every-green.name: UpperTheory.Top.every_character_of_green_v_win

imprimitive.title: Restore all characters
imprimitive.contract: ZeroFreeAll for primitive characters implies the all-moduli right-half-plane assertion with the principal pole exception.
imprimitive.idea: Use the change-of-level formula and nonvanishing of all finitely many additional Euler factors.
imprimitive.name: UpperTheory.Top.imprimitive

zero-green.title: Select the window width 3/2
zero-green.contract: Green, VWin and a nonempty definite-side package imply ZeroFreeAll.
zero-green.idea: Eliminate the nonempty package. Its shape supplies TopG and VWin supplies hosts for each primitive character.
zero-green.name: UpperTheory.Top.zero_free_all_of_green_v_win

shape.title: Choose a common geometric family
shape.contract: Green implies the specified TopShapeAlt ending in TopG.
shape.idea: Calls topDesWin with Cabs=2, C0=3, eD=2 and eL=0. This fixes both analytic loss exponents.
shape.name: UpperTheory.Top.shape_closed_link_n_of_green

family-design.title: Combine divisibility, slopes and windows
family-design.contract: The listed existence, local, rank, divisibility, global and slope controls produce FamilyClassConnected.
family-design.idea: Construct one family after taking a common epsilon threshold. Its loss exponents are the given eD and eL.
family-design.name: UpperTheory.Top.topDesWin

divin.title: Control the local divisibility loss
divin.contract: For ε>0, HypV, LinkN and SmallLevelRankEq imply DIVinN on the family.
divin.idea: Bound the weighted cohomology sum, replace the rank and absorb log²x into x^ε.
divin.name: UpperTheory.Top.divinN_of_hypV

vv-sum.title: Sum the local losses
vv-sum.contract: VVle gives finite cohomology lengths, summability and the bound on the infinite sum of vvTerm.
vv-sum.idea: Apply the bounded-partial-sums criterion to nonnegative prime contributions.
vv-sum.name: UpperTheory.Top.vvRecord

supply.title: Produce cyclic character hosts
supply.contract: For every primitive ψ, VWinAt ψ 401 implies host existence at width 3/2.
supply.idea: Use the window for the chosen character, then admissible twisted character classes on sufficiently large scales.
supply.name: UpperTheory.Top.supplyChi

vwin-row.title: Cohomological window from the row
vwin-row.contract: Row0b in the stated convention implies VWin.
vwin-row.idea: Pass an open-image record, the base-change theorem and the Galois row to the automorphic window construction.
vwin-row.name: UpperTheory.One.vwin_of_row

window-inputs.title: Supply the automorphic window inputs
window-inputs.contract: OpenImageCondition, BaseChangeIsobaricN and RowT imply VWin.
window-inputs.idea: Add the CM abelian inputs to the depth-zero residual base-change argument.
window-inputs.name: UpperTheory.One.Join.automorphic_window_of_inputs

depth-window.title: Build the rank-N package
depth-window.contract: The open-image, base-change, Galois and CM packages imply VWin.
depth-window.idea: Package local, automorphic, cohomological and CM inputs for the rank-N theorem.
depth-window.name: UpperTheory.One.Join.v_window_of_depth_zero_residual_bc_cm

lit-window.title: Window from rank-N automorphy
lit-window.idea: Invoke the automorphy-and-descent reduction for this rank-N package.
lit-window.name: UpperTheory.V.v_window_of_literal_automorphy_n

patch-window.title: Pass through the descent hypotheses
patch-window.idea: Combine the rank-N input with the weak descent theorem and the package produced by patching.
patch-window.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.DescentVanishingReductions.v_window_of_automorphy_csd_ss_mono_odd

four-produce.title: Produce the four counting bounds
four-produce.idea: Build the K bound, the descent inputs and counting cases I, II, III and V.
four-produce.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.DescentVanishingReductions.vwin_of_hypotheses_H_E_alt

four-use.title: Combine the cohomology counts
four-use.contract: Rank-N input, an existential K bound and CountI, CountII, CountIII, CountV imply VWin.
four-use.idea: Use local cohomological estimates, Ferrero–Washington and the additional terms in vwin_of_counts.
four-use.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.Core.of_four_alt

zero-top.title: Produce primitive zero-free levels
zero-top.contract: For λ>1, TopG and hosts for every primitive character imply ZeroFreeAll.
zero-top.idea: Combine the host supply, bound on tied families and the analytic criterion at each cyclic level.
zero-top.name: UpperTheory.Top.zeroFreeAll_of_topG

tied-cyc.title: Assemble the cyclic levels
tied-cyc.contract: Uniform window bounds, FormB, and family existence for cyclic levels imply ZeroFreeOn Q.
tied-cyc.idea: A primitive character belongs to its own cyclic level, so the level criterion covers it.
tied-cyc.name: Formalism.HC.zeroFreeOn_of_tiedWin_cyc

tied.title: Pass from levels to characters
tied.contract: Appropriate level data for each ψ satisfying Q imply ZeroFreeOn Q.
tied.idea: Extract the appropriate level and invoke level_of_tiedWin.
tied.name: Formalism.HC.zeroFreeOn_of_tiedWin

window-consumer.title: Choose epsilon after a candidate zero
window-consumer.contract: At any level, the chosen uniform arithmetic window and the analytic criterion imply zero-freeness right of one half.
window-consumer.idea: Take θ strictly between one half and the candidate real part, then choose ε with the loss exponent below θ.
window-consumer.name: Formalism.HC.level_of_tiedWin

prime-bound.title: The prime-sum inequality on tied families
prime-bound.contract: For every level, tied compatible families yield the windowed upper bound on the weighted prime sum.
prime-bound.idea: Translate ChainTied into the shared host data and call the Artin-input window theorem.
prime-bound.name: UpperTheory.Comparison₂.level_gm_le_on_family_scales

artin-window.title: Estimate the weighted level on a window
artin-window.contract: Identification of tied families with controlled host data gives ChebyshevInequalityOnWindows at any level.
artin-window.idea: Choose thresholds for the arithmetic and family estimates and obtain a compatible witness at each scale in the window.
artin-window.name: UpperTheory.Comparison₂.windowInequality_of_artinInputs

core-gm.title: From the height discrepancy to the prime sum
core-gm.contract: For large x, EAtH and CoreAtH imply G_P(x)≤x^(1/2+(eD+eL+7)ε).
core-gm.idea: Bound the per-index discrepancy, average via the character estimate and absorb the level-dependent factor into x^ε.
core-gm.name: UpperTheory.Comparison₂.core_gm

ch-top.title: Bound the discrepancy per index
ch-top.contract: The named identifications and size, error, and norm windows give an upper bound for gapA.
ch-top.idea: Write gapA as ASK minus Main, then combine the per-index estimate and the error bracket.
ch-top.name: Deduction.ch_top

ch-core.title: Average over characters
ch-core.contract: Under the size and character hypotheses, per-index discrepancy bounds imply a power bound for GmA up to SigA.
ch-core.idea: Character orthogonality and scale estimates convert the indexed bounds into a weighted average.
ch-core.name: Deduction.ch_core

form-b.title: The analytic criterion for a level
form-b.contract: For every level, every λ>1 and 0<θ<1, arbitrarily late windows bounded by x^θ imply no zero right of θ.
form-b.idea: Translate the level to a finite character family with positive weights. Apply the power-window theorem with δ=λ−1 and C=1.
form-b.name: UpperTheory.Comparison₂.formB

landau.title: The character-family power-window theorem
landau.contract: For a positive-weight family, a one-sided x^θ bound on arbitrarily late [Y,Y^(1+δ)] implies ZeroFree F θ.
landau.idea: Pass to the weighted-integral formulation of the Landau window criterion.
landau.name: Deduction.zeroFree_of_rpow_window

landau-lemma.title: Apply the pole obstruction
landau-lemma.contract: WindowHyp on a finite character family implies ZeroFree F θ in the given parameter range.
landau-lemma.idea: Build the pole data, exclude zeros in the strip by the window lemma, and use established nonvanishing at Re(s)≥1.
landau-lemma.name: Deduction.lemmaL

pole.title: Poles of the finite-family transform
pole.contract: For each admissible finite family there exists a transform with PoleData for its zero set.
pole.idea: Assemble individual character transforms and their pole data using positive weights.
pole.name: Deduction.poleData

oscillation.title: Rule out a pole right of θ
oscillation.contract: For the supplied PoleData and WindowHypU, any ρ in the specified pole set satisfies Re(ρ)≤θ.
oscillation.idea: Use high derivatives to compare a window upper bound with growth from an isolated pole.
oscillation.name: Deduction.landau_window

alternate-rh.title: A second zeta deduction
alternate-rh.idea: The alternate argument reflects completed zeta. The two zeta exports in Main use the other reducer.
alternate-rh.name: UpperTheory.riemannHypothesis_of_everyCharacter

rank.title: The geometric ranks
rank.contract: In particular, sqrt(x δ₁)≤m≤2 sqrt(x δ₁), with δ₁=x^(−ε/8).
rank.idea: The precise fixed-epsilon rank scale is x^(1/2−ε/16).
rank.name: GlobalTheory.EX.RankVal

minor.title: A local source of divisibility
minor.contract: For w²=p and the displayed congruences, w divides a two-by-two minor.
minor.idea: In the quotient by w the two transformed rows are multiples of one row. Their minor vanishes.
minor.name: Formalism.MainNotions.ColumnSystems.Pf.key_minor_dvd

behrend.title: Behrend’s collision-free indices
behrend.contract: For L≥1, encoding an integer sphere in base 4Ld gives a set with NoRel for coefficients bounded by L.
behrend.idea: The large base avoids carries. A line meets a sphere in at most two distinct points.
behrend.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.ThickExists.noRel_image

empty-data.title: An existence check on a period identity
empty-data.contract: At a suitable intermediate stage there exists v≠0 such that level volume times character weight equals v at every admissible datum.
empty-data.idea: Haar measure times index is constant. When the permitted datum set is empty the theorem explicitly chooses v=1.
empty-data.name: GlobalTheory.Fam.volLev_mul_wt_mid_alt

slope.title: The lattice slope inequality
slope.contract: The sublattice bound SlopeLeMuMax implies SlopeInequality for injective norm-bounded lattice maps.
slope.idea: A Gram determinant bounds the image covolume by C to the rank times the source covolume.
slope.name: Formalism.F.slopeInequality_of

paper-chain.title: The square-root multiplicity analogy
paper-chain.contract: The author describes repeated theta lifts as a number-field analogue of multiplicity in the function-field argument.
paper-chain.idea: The first page motivates taking a chain on the square-root scale.

paper-behrend.title: The tower selection in the timeline
paper-behrend.contract: Entry 19 links the choice of a tower to Behrend-type sets.
paper-behrend.idea: The author singles out an additive-combinatorial construction in the choice of the tower.

tower-window-from-lemma-k.title: Assemble the arithmetic tower window
tower-window-from-lemma-k.contract: One package of constants works at every cutoff exponent Ct ≥ 1.
tower-window-from-lemma-k.idea: Apply the cohomological bound to each eligible tower. Ferrero–Washington supplies the generator bounds for the fixed odd primes and the varying two-adic bases. Pass both estimates and the uniform H² bound to the window construction.
tower-window-from-lemma-k.name: UpperTheory.V.Win.thmBab_of_lemmaK

tower-window-constants.title: Choose one set of tower constants
tower-window-constants.contract: There exists a single BConst K such that every Ct ≥ 1 satisfies ThmBab K Ct.
tower-window-constants.idea: Choose the uniform two-adic rank and the ranks of the eligible odd-prime towers before the scale and auxiliary prime pair. Unite the exceptional twists and find a single interval avoiding their forbidden ranges.
tower-window-constants.name: UpperTheory.V.Win.thmBab_of

tower-bound-from-rank.title: From a finitely generated tower to two length bounds
tower-bound-from-rank.contract: For each prime and eligible tower, ABound consists of a bound away from finitely many centres and a bound in terms of a fixed layer.
tower-bound-from-rank.idea: Choose a Galois element generating the cyclotomic direction, prove the descent equality for its twists, and apply the two cokernel estimates on the tower module.
tower-bound-from-rank.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.aBound_of_isTower

tower-operator-bound.title: Control exceptional twists by the fixed layer
tower-operator-bound.contract: The lengths are controlled by at most R ℓ-adic centres. For all twists they are also bounded by the fixed-layer H² length plus R times the excess layer index.
tower-operator-bound.idea: Use unipotence modulo ℓ and the generator bound for the centres. The relative growth estimate can allow infinite length at a singular twist. Descent and duality bound the reference value by the arithmetic H² length.
tower-operator-bound.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.aBound_of_descends

tower-class-rank.title: Uniform ℓ-rank of class groups in the tower
tower-class-rank.contract: For each eligible abelian base K and prime ℓ there is an exponent r bounding the order of the quotient by ℓ-th powers by ℓʳ on every cyclotomic layer.
tower-class-rank.idea: Embed the abelian base into a cyclotomic field. Use the cyclotomic index estimate and descend across a uniformly bounded degree. The root-of-unity premise in the published interface is unused by this proof.
tower-class-rank.name: UpperTheory.V.FW.ferreroWashington

tower-fixed-growth.title: Supply the absolute bound for the reference layer
tower-fixed-growth.contract: One real exponent bounds the logarithm of the order of $H^2(G_{L,S},\mathbb Z_\ell(e+1))$ over all eligible fields, coefficient primes and positive twists. Each such group is finite.
tower-fixed-growth.idea: Insert the odd-degree integral homology rank estimate into the reduction from the rank-N package. The resulting LemmaK bound may be applied at the fixed layer even when the abstract cokernel estimate allows infinite length.
tower-fixed-growth.name: UpperTheory.V.ZK.lemmaK_litN_alt

counts-i.title: Case I gives one bound across coefficient primes
counts-i.contract: Away from the exceptional set, when ℓ−1 does not divide twice the twist, the sum over every allowed finite set of coefficient primes obeys one polynomial bound.
counts-i.idea: Combine a rank-three eigensystem count with a single-character rigidity bound. Their common integer bounds the local lengths by its valuations. Two auxiliary primes then cover all the coefficient primes.
counts-i.name: UpperTheory.V.Z.J.count_i_of_printed_bound_k_kato_automorphy

counts-ii-iii.title: Cases II and III from the rank-four symplectic argument
counts-ii-iii.contract: Cases II and III have uniform polynomial bounds for each normalized character length, with finiteness. The hypotheses distinguish parity of character orders and divisibility of twice the twist.
counts-ii-iii.idea: Supply the symplectic rigidity and eigensystem-counting inputs to the same rank-four theorem. The cohomological hypotheses and LemmaK provide the finite local lengths used in its two outputs.
counts-ii-iii.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.DescentVanishingReductions.countII_and_countIII_of_printsH_of_sp4In

counts-v.title: Case V at twist one
counts-v.contract: For exceptional odd primes at twist one, Case V bounds the normalized length when the two-adic conductor crosses the specified threshold, including equality.
counts-v.idea: Pass a reduced unitary lift, local and global cohomological estimates, host rigidity and a host parameter count to the rank-three inertia argument. The strict reverse threshold is covered by a separate case.
counts-v.name: UpperTheory.V.Z.J.count_v_of_printed_bound_k_reduced_unitary_lift

counts-common-integer.title: A nonzero integer controls one character orbit
counts-common-integer.contract: For a fixed imaginary quadratic field, twist, character kernel and admissible auxiliary prime, one nonzero integer gives a logarithmic size bound and simultaneous valuation bounds at the other eligible primes.
counts-common-integer.idea: Make a Galois-stable family of characters with the chosen kernel. A trace product supplies the integer before the coefficient prime is chosen. Rigidity bounds the sum of the orbit lengths by twice its valuation.
counts-common-integer.name: UpperTheory.V.Z.J.propGK_of_numberU3U_of_oneCharU

counts-window.title: Convert the joint window into VWin
counts-window.contract: The tower window, sign bounds and five counting inputs yield VWin, the cohomology estimate for each primitive character at cutoff exponent 401.
counts-window.idea: Obtain a common tower and positive-part window, convert the negative-part bound at exponent 401, and combine the contributions on the same interval.
counts-window.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.vwin_of_counts

counts-joint.title: Reuse the tower interval for the positive part
counts-joint.contract: For each eligible choice of character and parameters, one interval satisfies both the tower and positive-part bounds at every point.
counts-joint.idea: Apply the height estimate to the very interval selected by ThmBab. Its universal quantifier over accepted windows permits this reuse.
counts-joint.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.jointWin_of_counts

counts-height.title: Evaluate the pointwise estimate on admissible windows
counts-height.contract: Every package K and positive cutoff exponent Ct satisfy the positive-part height theorem under the stated counting and cohomology inputs.
counts-height.idea: First prove the estimate with layer bounds as hypotheses. The height theorem specializes it using the supplied interval, the primes, the cutoff and the very same field.
counts-height.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.thmHV_of_counts

counts-pointwise.title: Combine the two prime sums at a point
counts-pointwise.contract: After the character and layer indices are fixed, one polynomial bound controls the positive cohomological sum on eligible hosts, with an additive multiple of the layer budget.
counts-pointwise.idea: Form separate sums inside and outside the fixed exceptional set. Inside, the dispatcher also supplies Case IV and the strict-threshold case Vs. Add the two estimates using the same host and layer budget.
counts-pointwise.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.pointHV_of_counts

counts-inside.title: Add contributions inside the exceptional set
counts-inside.contract: For fixed character, exceptional coefficient prime and layer index, the positive-part sum at that prime is at most (Nt)^C + C·B when the fixed layer satisfies its budget B.
counts-inside.idea: Separate the twist-one threshold from the higher twists. For the odd-order branch, Case IV uses the supplied layer bound. Absorb the finite character contributions into a common exponent.
counts-inside.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.sumIn

counts-outside.title: Bound the sum over arbitrary finite sets of other primes
counts-outside.contract: Choose a common exponent and two auxiliary primes before the host. The positive-part sum over every allowed finite set of nonexceptional odd primes is at most (Nt)^C.
counts-outside.idea: Apply Case I to the unrestricted contribution. For the remainder ℓ−1 divides twice the twist, bounding the number of relevant primes. Cases Z, II and III and the character counts control these terms.
counts-outside.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.sumOut

moment-target.title: The first moment of the Chebyshev error
moment-target.contract: The truncated integral of (ψ(t)−t)/t² from 1 to U tends to −1−γ as U tends to infinity.
moment-target.idea: This is an improper-integral limit for the real von Mangoldt sum. It fixes the coefficient of the linear centering term in the reading converse.
moment-target.name: Formalism.HermitianLattices.GL2a2.PsiZeroConst

moment-theorem.title: Evaluate the first moment
moment-theorem.contract: The archive supplies its first-moment limit without an RH assumption.
moment-theorem.idea: The public theorem calls the source-level proof psiZeroConst_main. This separate theorem helps explain the reverse implication for the singleton zeta family.
moment-theorem.name: Formalism.HermitianLattices.GL2a2.psi_zero_integral_constant

moment-calculation.title: Match the two limits at one
moment-calculation.contract: For the trivial character modulo one the Chebyshev remainder has first moment −1−γ.
moment-calculation.idea: Evaluate the Mellin integral for real σ>1 in terms of the logarithmic derivative of zeta. The remainder bound allows passage to σ=1. The finite part of the logarithmic derivative fixes the value.
moment-calculation.name: psiZeroConst_main

moment-majorant.title: Dominate the centered character sum
moment-majorant.contract: For each fixed character, the centered von Mangoldt sum is eventually bounded in norm by Kt/log²t.
moment-majorant.idea: The Siegel–Walfisz estimate applies at a fixed modulus for all sufficiently large t. Exponential decay in the square root of log t implies the displayed inverse logarithmic factor.
moment-majorant.name: sw_bound

moment-dominated.title: Pass the Mellin integral to σ = 1
moment-dominated.contract: A logarithmic remainder bound lets σ times the weighted integral tend to its value at σ=1 from the right.
moment-dominated.idea: The local integrand is measurable. A bound by the integrable error at σ=1 gives dominated convergence. The factor σ tends to one.
moment-dominated.name: core_tendsto

moment-laurent.title: Read Euler’s constant from the logarithmic derivative
moment-laurent.contract: As complex s tends puncturedly to 1, ζ′(s)/ζ(s)+1/(s−1) tends to γ.
moment-laurent.idea: Remove the pole by putting g(s)=(s−1)ζ(s) and g(1)=1. The quotient g′/g tends to γ and agrees with the regularized logarithmic derivative off the pole.
moment-laurent.name: zeta_logderiv_limit

itineraries.title: Read the last page of the proof first
itineraries.question: How does a right-half-plane estimate imply ordinary RH?

itineraries.title: Find the mathematical estimate
itineraries.question: How wide must the intervals be, and where does the loss in the exponent come from?

itineraries.title: Find who supplies the arithmetic
itineraries.question: Which assertion has to produce the compatible Galois, theta and cohomology data?

itineraries.title: Follow a singular twist and an arbitrary finite prime sum
itineraries.question: Which bound controls a twist of unbounded abstract length, and how can one estimate work over every allowed finite set of coefficient primes?

itineraries.title: Recover the centering constant in the ordinary zeta window
itineraries.question: Why is the linear correction (1+γ)x?
